questions.question: Which of the following minerals is NOT found in rivers (alluvial placers) and on the coast, especially beaches (beach placers)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Bauxite.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The main minerals and metals associated with placer deposits are gold, cassiterite (tin), platinum, diamonds, magnetite, and some gemstones.
 
• The two most important kinds of placers are stream (alluvial) and beach placers.
 
 
• Hence Bauxite is the correct answer.
 
 
 
• Beach placers are formed in sand and gravel deposited along the edge of large bodies of water and are typically found where streams or rivers flow into a large body of water.
 
• Materials gather as beach placers by continuous wave action and currents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bauxite is a sedimentary rock with a relatively high aluminium content.
 
• It is the world's main source of aluminium and gallium.
 
• Bauxite is a naturally happen, heterogeneous material composed primarily of one or more aluminium hydroxide minerals, plus various mixtures of silica, iron oxide, titania, aluminosilicate, and other impurities in minor or trace amounts.
 
• The main uses of bauxite are multipurpose covering metallurgy, chemical industries, as raw material in building and road aggregates.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice-President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 66.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to Article 66 of the Constitution of India**, the **Vice-President is elected by the members of the Electoral College consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.**
 
• Article 66 of the Constitution of India states the** manner of election of the vice president.**
 
• Whenever there is a vacancy in the **office of the Vice President,** the** President shall nominate a Vice President who shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.**
 
• **Article 58 of the constitution sets the principal qualifications one must meet to be eligible **for the office of the president. A president must be a citizen of India. **of 35 years of age or above.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 68_​ ** An election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of Vice-President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
 
• **Article 64**_The Vice-President shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States and shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• **Article 62_**An election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.

questions.question: The body of animals of the phylum Protozoa, such as Paramecium, Amoeba, Euglena, shows ________ grade organisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protoplasmic.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Protozoa is a phylum having **unicellular heterotrophs**. It comes under Kingdom Protista.
 
• A protozoan body consists of only a mass of protoplasm, so they are called acellular or non-cellular animals. Grade of organization: **protoplasmic grade of organization**.
 
• **Single-cell performs all the vital activities thus the single cell acts** like a whole body. The body** of protozoa is either naked or covered by a pellicle.**
 
• Protozoa can be divided into four phyla based on their locomotion: **Mastigophora, Sarcodina, Ciliophora, and Sporozoa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b1149550084fd4e895543d9f40fb390a035a2a2e0b6f723b3f1bed13d404409.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tissue-organ**_​ The organ level of organization is **when two or more tissues work together for a specific function**. For example, **the bladder consists of an inner lining of epithelial tissue, bound by various connective tissues to (smooth) muscle.**
 
• Most organisms have functional parts with five levels: **cells, tissues, organs, organ systems and whole organisms**.
 
• "Cellular organization" is **the defining property in living organisms.**

questions.question: According to Mendeleev's periodic table, which unknown element of group III had an atomic mass of 68 that was later replaced by gallium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eka–aluminum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It was later discovered as Aluminium with an **atomic weight of 68 and an atomic number of 31. Germanium was named as ****Aka-Silicon first and was later discovered.**
 
• Eka prefix means that element occurring after suffix atom. It Means Eka aluminium is Gallium and Eka silicon is Germanium.
 
• One of these elements was the element now called Germanium; Mendeleev called it “eka-silicon,” meaning “beyond silicon” on his table.
 
• The existence of germanium was predicted by Dimitri Mendeleev in 1869 from a blank space in his periodic table beneath silicon; hence the term eka-silicon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6e0f4a473a5595c90984bc3f6183e95e85475b2b5ca3a6d6f2e1afba5f12e3b.png]

• Eka-aluminium was the name given by Mendeleev to the undiscovered element which now exists by the name of Gallium. Gallium belongs to group 13 of the periodic table. Its atomic number is 31 with the sign Ga. It is a soft, silvery metal at standard temperature and pressure.
 
• **Ekaboron (uncountable) (chemistry) is the name given by Dmitri Mendeleev to the predicted element (scandium) lying below the boron in the periodic table.**

questions.question:
Which of the following is an objective of the Government Budget?

(A) GDP growth

(B) Reallocation of resources

(C) Balanced regional growth
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__A, B and C.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The various objectives of the government budget are:**

 
 
• ​Reallocation of Resources.
 
• Reducing inequalities in income and wealth.
 
• Economic Stability.
 
• Management of Public Enterprises.
 
• Economic Growth.
 
• Reducing regional disparities.
 
 
• **Hence A, B, and C statements are correct. **
 
 
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****

 
• A government budget is a document prepared by the government and/or other political entity presenting its anticipated tax revenues and proposed spending/expenditure for the coming financial year.
 
• In most parliamentary systems, the budget is presented to the legislature and often requires the approval of the legislature.
 
• **The three types of annual Government budgets based on estimates are:**
 
 
• ​Surplus Budget.
 
• Balanced Budget.
 
• Deficit Budget.

__
 
• **Anton Van Leeuwenhoek** is universally acknowledged as the father of **microbiology.**
 
• He discovered both **protists and bacteria.**
 
• In 1674 he likely observed protozoa for the first time and several years later bacteria. 
 
• Those** “very little animalcules”** he was able to isolate from different sources, such as** rainwater, pond, well water, and the human mouth and intestine.** He also calculated their sizes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Brown **FRSE FRS FLS MWS was a Scottish botanist and paleobotanist who made important contributions to botany largely through his pioneering use of the microscope. 
 
• **Robert Hooke** FRS was an English polymath active as a scientist and architect, who, using a microscope, was the first to visualize a micro-organism.
 
• **Rudolf Ludwig Carl Virchow **was a German physician, anthropologist, pathologist, prehistorian, biologist, writer, editor, and politician. 
 
• He is known as** "the father of modern pathology"** and as the founder of social medicine, and to his colleagues, the "Pope of medicine".

• **​__**The Padma Awards are **one of the highest civilian honours of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day**.
 
• The Awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of higher order) and Padma Shri (distinguished service).

• **All persons without distinction of race, occupation, position or sex** are eligible for these Awards.

questions.question: Why does the effective nuclear charge experienced by valence electrons decrease down the group?

options.text: The outermost electrons are closest to the nucleus
innermost electrons are farther away from the nucleus
outermost electrons are farther away from the nucleus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __the outermost electrons are further away from the nucleus.____ __

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __key points__

__
 
• Down the group, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the valence electrons decreases as the outermost electrons move further away from the nucleus .
 
• These electrons can be easily lost. 
 
• Thus, the metallic property decreases in a period and moves down the group.
 
• The effective nuclear charge increases in period from left to right as the table unfolds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• The word "effective" is used because shielding effect The negatively charged electron prevents the higher energy electrons from experiencing the full nuclear charge of the nucleus due to the repulsive effect of the inner layer. 
 
• The effective nuclear charge experienced by an electron is also called the core charge.
 
• A higher effective nuclear charge causes greater attraction for electrons, pulling the electron cloud closer to the nucleus resulting in a smaller atomic radius.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of 'A Movable Feast'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ernest Hemingway__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A Moveable Feast is a 1964 memoir Belles-Letres by American author Ernest Hemingway.
 
• The book is about his years as a struggling ex-pat journalist and author in Paris during the 1920s. It was published posthumously.
 
• Hemingway left behind a substantial amount of manuscripts, some of which have been published. 
 
• A Moveable Feast, a gripping memoir of his years in Paris (1921–26) before he became famous, was released in 1964.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Ernest Miller Hemingway was an American novelist, short-story writer, and journalist.
 
• His economical and understated style—what he called the iceberg theory— had a strong influence on 20th-century fiction , while his adventurous lifestyle and public image earned him praise from later generations.
 
• He was best known for novels such as The Sun Also Rises, A Farewell to Arms, For Whom the Bell Tolls and The Old Man and the Sea, which won the Pulitzer Prize in 1953.
 
• In 1954, Hemingway won the Nobel Prize. He committed suicide on July 2, 1961, in Ketchum, Idaho.
